chunks: With this chain of narration, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is affected by janābah in a cold land and cannot find water, and it may be that the water is frozen,
So he said: "He should perform ghusl in whatever manner is possible."
A man told him that he had done that and became ill for a month because of the cold,
So he said: "He performed ghusl in whatever manner was possible, for there is no escaping ghusl."
And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام mentioned that he had been compelled to it while he was ill, so they brought it to him warmed, and he performed ghusl. And he said: "There is no escaping ghusl."

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the obligatory ritual bath in the context of janābah
key_terms.الْمَاءُ جَامِدًا: water that is frozen or solid due to cold
key_terms.بَارِدَةٍ: severely cold conditions affecting the performance of purification
key_terms.مُسَخَّنًا: warmed, referring to water heated for use
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ghusl for janābah in extreme cold when water is frozen or difficult to use?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of ghusl in severe cold and difficult conditions. It indicates the necessity of ghusl for janābah when possible, even if water must be warmed or used under hardship. The report is significant in discussions of ritual purity and the limits of hardship in acts of worship.
